raw_signature: nullreferenceexception|object reference not set to an instance
plain_translation: Something you are using has not been set yet, so Unity has nothing to work with.
checklist_fixes: Check the error line , which variable is null? Add a null check: if(obj != null) .
Make sure you assigned the reference in the Inspector (drag the object into the field).
Check that GetComponent<T>() actually found the component , it returns null if not found.
Don't access a GameObject after Destroy() , it's null after destruction.
problem_html: Unity throws "NullReferenceException: Object reference not set to an instance of an object" and your code stops.
prevention_html: Use [SerializeField] private T field; and assign in Inspector. Or use FindObjectOfType<T>() in Awake(). Always null-check before using.
keywords: null reference exception object reference not set destroyed missing NullReferenceException unassigned reference

plain_translation: The Inspector field is empty. Drag the object in, or find it in code before using it.
checklist_fixes: Drag the GameObject from the Hierarchy into the Inspector field on your script.
For components, drag the object that has the component (Unity finds it automatically).
If the field is private, add [SerializeField] to expose it in the Inspector.
Check the field type matches what you're dragging , e.g. a Transform, not a GameObject.
problem_html: A script field shows "None (GameObject)" in the Inspector. The code can't find the component it needs.
prevention_html: Use [SerializeField] on private fields so you can drag-assign while keeping encapsulation. Never leave Inspector fields as None at runtime.
keywords: component not assigned missing inspector drag drop

plain_translation: Physics is being moved in the wrong update, so the object fights itself every frame.
checklist_fixes: Use FixedUpdate() for physics code, Update() for input-only code.
Use Time.deltaTime when moving with transform.position , not with Rigidbody.
For Rigidbody movement, use AddForce() or set velocity directly , not transform.position.
Increase Rigidbody interpolation: set Interpolate to "Interpolate" in the Inspector.
problem_html: Your object shakes or jitters when moving. The movement looks jerky and unstable.
prevention_html: Rule of thumb: position changes via transform → Update(). Force-based movement via Rigidbody → FixedUpdate(). Never mix the two.
keywords: physics jitter shaking movement rb addforce rigidbody

plain_translation: The scene file has moved or its path is wrong, so Godot cannot load it.
checklist_fixes: Add the scene to Build Settings: File → Build Settings → Add Open Scenes.
Use the exact scene name as shown in the Hierarchy (no path, no .unity extension).
Make sure using UnityEngine.SceneManagement; is at the top of the script.
Check you're not loading a scene that doesn't exist in the build list.
problem_html: SceneManager.LoadScene("SceneName") does nothing or throws an error. The scene won't switch.
prevention_html: Use scene build indices: LoadScene(1) instead of names. Add all scenes to Build Settings as you create them.
keywords: scene not loading scene management build settings loadscene
